Phoenix Airport Shuttle for Groups

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private Phoenix airport shuttle from Sky Harbor for groups of 14 to 56 with their luggage: the whole vehicle is reserved for your party, with no other passengers and no shared stops. A shuttle trip is $295 to $1,250 per vehicle before 8% Arizona sales tax, from the Executive Black Sprinter at $295 (about $21 a seat when full) to the 56-Passenger Motorcoach at $1,250, and a 50% deposit holds the date.

Last updated: October 1, 2026

Landing with a smaller party, or on your own? See PHX-to-Scottsdale private SUV and Sprinter transfers.

Is this a shared airport shuttle?

No. Scottsdale Sprinters runs private group shuttles out of Phoenix Sky Harbor: you reserve the whole vehicle for your own party, it makes no stops for anyone else, and the price is per vehicle rather than per seat. Scottsdale Sprinters holds the Phoenix Sky Harbor (PHX) ground transportation permit. That changes the arithmetic for a group. A shared-ride van charges each traveller and collects other passengers on the way; a private shuttle charges one trip price however many of your seats you fill, so the cost per head falls as the group grows. It also means the shuttle leaves when your group is together, with your bags, and goes to the addresses you gave.

What are the Phoenix airport shuttle rates for a group?

Published shuttle trips run $295 to $1,250 depending on the vehicle, before 8% Arizona sales tax. A shuttle trip is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and a longer one is priced from the drive with the empty return included; the quote shows which applies. Executive Black Sprinter: 14 seats and room for 40 bags, $295 a trip, about $21 a seat when every seat is filled. Executive White Sprinter: 14 seats and room for 40 bags, $295 a trip, about $21 a seat when every seat is filled. Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax): 27 seats and room for 40 bags, $550 a trip, about $20 a seat when every seat is filled. Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax): 29 seats and room for 30 bags, $550 a trip, about $19 a seat when every seat is filled. 56-Passenger Motorcoach: 56 seats and room for 125 bags, $1,250 a trip, about $22 a seat when every seat is filled. The per-seat figure is the trip price divided by the seats, for planning a group budget only: you pay for the vehicle, not the headcount. Book the return to the airport on the same reservation and the 20% return credit applies, so the Executive Black Sprinter back to Sky Harbor is $236 rather than $295.

Which shuttle fits our group and its luggage?

Count seats and suitcases separately, then take the smallest shuttle that clears both. The shuttles on this page seat 14 to 56, and every one of them carries a published bag count. Up to 14 travellers fit an Executive Black Sprinter with room for 40 bags. Past that, the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax) seats 27 with room for 40 bags and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) seats 29 with room for 30 bags. The 56-Passenger Motorcoach takes 56 and has underfloor bays for 125 bags, the one vehicle for a whole flight's worth of a group. The Maybach Shuttle Sprinter and the Mini Bus (24 Pax) are left off this page on purpose: without a luggage figure we can publish, they are not sold as an airport shuttle. Golf bags, strollers and oversized cases go on the manifest by name.

Our flights land at different times. One shuttle or several runs?

Two ways work. Book each arrival wave as its own shuttle trip at the trip price, or reserve the shuttle by the hour so it waits at the airport and collects each flight in turn. Separate trips suit two or three waves spread across the day: each run is its own trip price, and a small wave can take a smaller vehicle than the big one. The hourly block suits waves that land close together, or a group that wants one vehicle standing by: rate times billable hours, never below the vehicle's own minimum. The Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) is $225 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, a $900 block before tax, against $550 for a single trip. Either way, give us every flight on the manifest. Flight tracking is included on airport work, and how a late arrival changes the pickup is stated in your written quote.

Can one booking cover more than one shuttle?

Yes, for the shuttles we run more than one of. A single reservation takes up to 3 of the same unit, so 3 Executive Mini Coaches move 87 seated travellers together. The units a booking can multiply are the Executive Black Sprinters, Executive White Sprinters, Grech Mini Buses and Executive Mini Coaches. The 56-Passenger Motorcoach is one of a kind, so a group bigger than it adds a second vehicle on its own reservation. At 20 or more passengers a booking sits in the large-group cancellation tier, so read that tier before you confirm.

What goes on a group shuttle manifest?

Six things: each flight's airline and number with the headcount on it, the total bag count, the drop-off address for every hotel or home in the group, any stop on the way, the name of the person meeting the shuttle, and a mobile number that will be answered on the day. Send the manifest with the quote request and update it if a flight changes. An added stop on a shuttle trip is $50; a greeter who meets the group at baggage claim with a name sign and helps with the bags is $200 and is optional. The pickup instruction for your terminal comes from the chauffeur, and the confirmation states which pickup method you booked.

Who books a private group shuttle from the airport?

The arrivals that fill a shuttle are the ones where a whole group lands for one reason: a conference or company offsite, a wedding weekend with guests on several flights, a golf trip, and a team or school travelling together. Each has its own page below with its own vehicles and packages. For a wedding, put the guest shuttle both ways on one reservation so the return credit applies; for a conference, book the arrival day and the departure day as two trips; for golf, count the clubs as bags. The shuttle is the same vehicle in every case; the manifest is what changes.

Do you also run shuttles from Scottsdale Airport and Mesa Gateway?

Yes. A Scottsdale Airport arrival is booked on the same kind of reservation and quoted from the same vehicles, and Phoenix-Mesa Gateway (AZA) has its own group transportation page, linked below, for the east-side arrival.

How do the deposit, balance and cancellation work?

How the rest settles depends on how you pay: on a card, a 50% deposit holds the date and your written confirmation sets out the balance and its timing; paying in full at checkout leaves nothing else due before your ride; a payment link from the reservations desk opens that same checkout. 8% Arizona sales tax is added at checkout. There is no booking fee and no fuel surcharge on the trip price. Cancellation terms are tiered by trip type and group size and are published in full on the policies page. For a question before you book, call or text (623) 986-6339 or email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a shuttle from Phoenix airport to Scottsdale?

Yes. Scottsdale Sprinters runs private group shuttles from Phoenix Sky Harbor to Scottsdale and across the Valley, reserved for your party alone. The Executive Black Sprinter is $295 a trip for up to 14 travellers with room for 40 bags, before 8% tax. A shuttle trip is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and a longer one is priced from the drive with the empty return included; the quote shows which applies.

How much is a private shuttle from Sky Harbor for a large group?

Scottsdale Sprinters prices a group shuttle per vehicle: $295 for the Executive Black Sprinter (14 seats), $295 for the Executive White Sprinter (14 seats), $550 for the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax) (27 seats), $550 for the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) (29 seats) and $1,250 for the 56-Passenger Motorcoach (56 seats), before tax. Filled to every seat, that is about $22 a traveller on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach.

Does Phoenix Sky Harbor have a shared shuttle?

Shared-ride shuttles operate at Sky Harbor on their own schedules and tariffs, which we do not quote. Scottsdale Sprinters does not sell seats on a shared van: every shuttle we send is reserved for one group, so it waits for your party and makes only your stops.

Can I get a shuttle from Phoenix airport to my hotel?

Yes. A Scottsdale Sprinters shuttle goes to the addresses on your manifest: a hotel, a rental home or an office, one stop or several. Put each address on the request, and add $50 for every stop on the way. A shuttle trip is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and a longer one is priced from the drive with the empty return included; the quote shows which applies.

Does a private airport shuttle run on a schedule?

No. A Scottsdale Sprinters shuttle is booked for your group, so it runs to your flights rather than to a timetable: give the airline and flight number for every arrival, and your written confirmation states the pickup method, the meeting point and a day-of contact.

What if one of our flights is delayed?

Flight tracking is included on airport work with Scottsdale Sprinters, and how a delayed flight changes the pickup is stated in your written quote. For several flights landing close together, reserve the shuttle by the hour and it waits for each one: the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) is $225 per hour on a 4-hour minimum.

How many suitcases fit in an airport shuttle?

Scottsdale Sprinters publishes a bag figure for every shuttle: 40 in the Executive Black Sprinter, 40 in the Executive White Sprinter, 40 in the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), 30 in the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and 125 in the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Give the bag count with the headcount when you book.

Can we book the shuttle back to the airport as well?

Yes. Put the departure on the same reservation and Scottsdale Sprinters takes 20% off the return leg: $1,000 rather than $1,250 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach, for example.

Can we book more than one shuttle for a big group?

Yes. One Scottsdale Sprinters reservation takes up to 3 of the same shuttle where we run more than one, which is up to 87 seats on Executive Mini Coaches. The 56-Passenger Motorcoach is a single unit, so it is booked on its own.

Do we pay a deposit for a group airport shuttle?

How the rest settles depends on how you pay: on a card, a 50% deposit holds the date and your written confirmation sets out the balance and its timing; paying in full at checkout leaves nothing else due before your ride; a payment link from the reservations desk opens that same checkout. 8% Arizona sales tax is added at checkout.

Is one private Sprinter cheaper than two Uber XLs from Sky Harbor?

The Scottsdale Sprinters Executive Black Sprinter is $295 one way for up to 14 travellers with room for 40 bags, before 8% tax. A shuttle trip is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and a longer one is priced from the drive with the empty return included; the quote shows which applies. Shared, that is about $30 a person for 10 riders, $25 for 12 and $21 for 14. Rideshare is priced by the app at request time, so the comparison is made on the day; Uber's own page says UberXL takes parties of up to 6, so 12 travellers fill two XLs and 14 need 3.

Can you move 30 conference attendees from Sky Harbor at once?

Yes, on one Scottsdale Sprinters booking of up to 3 of the same shuttle: 3 Executive Black Sprinters (42 seats, room for 120 bags) at $295 each one way, about $885 in all; or 2 Executive Mini Coaches (58 seats, room for 60 bags) at $550 each one way, about $1,100 in all, before tax. A shuttle trip is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and a longer one is priced from the drive with the empty return included; the quote shows which applies.
